Hadhrat Ali (RA) then turned to Hadhrat Abul Aswad Duwali and said, "All types of non-Arabs are entering into the fold of Islaam, so include something (in the Qur'aanic script) by which they may receive guidance to recite properly." It was then that the Fatha, Dhamma and Kasra[^1] were written. [^2]
For A Leader to Appoint someone to Teach the People

Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ left for Hunayn, he appointed Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) over the people of Makkah with instructions to teach the Qur'aan to the people and to create an understanding of Deen amongst them. Thereafter, when Rasulullaah ﷺ left for Madinah, he again appointed Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) over the people of Makkah. [^3]

Hadhrat Mujaahid narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) over the people of Makkah when he left for Hunayn so that he should create an understanding of Deen amongst them and teach them the Qur'aan. [^4]
Can a Leader Prevent Someone from Proceeding in the path of Allaah for the sake of Knowledge?
Hadhrat Umar (RA) Confines Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) in Madinah to Teach the People

Hadhrat Qaasim narrates that whenever Hadhrat Umar (RA) left on a journey, he would leave Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) as his deputy in Madinah. Whereas Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to dispatch men to various cities (for teaching), he would send Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) only for the most vital tasks (but would otherwise keep him in Madinah). When requests were made (by the people of the various Islaamic territories) to send specific people and Hadhrat Zaid (RA) was asked for by name, Hadhrat Umar (RA) would say, "Zaid's status in my estimation has not fallen at all. I keep him back only because the people of Madinah need Zaid in the matters they encounter and cannot get from anyone else what they get from him." [^5]

Hadhrat Saalim bin Abdullaah says, "We were with Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) the day Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) passed away. 'A great Aalim has passed away today,' I remarked.
